title: Evaporative Emissions Diagnostic Routing
introduction:
The evaporative emissions system (EVAP) handles fuel vapor so it can later be used by the engine. Vapor control and liquid-fuel delivery have different jobs; a vapor-system code alone does not put the fuel pump in the guilty seat.

I use this page as a fork in the diagnostic road: a powertrain control module (PCM) diagnostic trouble code (DTC) leads to engine-control diagnosis, while driveability symptoms without a code lead to symptom charts. The named references contain the actual diagnostic work; this page does not supply the tests or authorize a parts replacement.

edits.text: For a diagnostic trouble code (DTC) in the powertrain control module (PCM), refer to [Electronic Engine Controls](#/document/G1692929) (303-14A Electronic Engine Controls - 2.3L EcoBoost (231kW/314PS), Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: This branch takes a PCM code to the diagnostic information for the specified engine configuration. The code selects a diagnostic route rather than proving a component has failed.

edits.text: For driveability symptoms without a DTC, refer to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED) manual, Section 3, Symptom Charts.
edits.why: The absence of a code does not dismiss the complaint. It changes the next reference to the symptom-based diagnostic charts.
